What Is the Super Bowl?

The NFL has been in existence since 1920, and a championship game has been a part of every season since 1932.

However, the first Super Bowl did not take place until more than three decades later.

In 1960, the American Football League began and soon emerged as a serious rival to the NFL. The leagues eventually elected to merge, with the creation of the Super Bowl a result of the planned merger.

The first four Super Bowls were pre-merger, with the first taking place to end the 1966 season. On January 15, 1967, the NFL champion Green Bay Packers defeated the AFL champion Kansas City Chiefs 35-10 at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

Since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970, the Super Bowl matchup has featured the champions of the NFL’s two conferences, the AFC (which partially consists of former AFL teams) and the NFC.

The NFL playoffs determine the conference champions. Under the current NFL playoff format, seven teams in each conference take part in the playoffs. The playoffs consist of three rounds: the wild-card round, the divisional round, and the conference championship round.

Super Bowl venues, which are all current NFL stadiums, are determined years in advance. Super Bowl 60 will take place on February 8, 2026, at Levi’s Stadium, the home of the San Francisco 49ers.

The game is seen as a neutral-site game, but a team can play in the Super Bowl at home. That occurred for the first time in Super Bowl 55, when Tom Brady and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated the Chiefs at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, and the following year, when the Los Angeles Rams defeated the Cincinnati Bengals in Super Bowl 56 at SoFi Stadium.

Types of Super Bowl Bets

As the popular saying goes, variety is the spice of life. Variety is also the name of the game when it comes to Super Bowl betting as well.

As it is, there are plenty of options if you bet on NFL games during the regular season or playoffs.

But the Super Bowl is an entirely different animal altogether. And if you are not that familiar with how to bet on the NFL or how to bet on sports in general, trying to navigate the options you have to choose from can be an arduous task.

The types of Super Bowl bets mentioned in this guide are the main types of bets to look out for if you bet on the upcoming matchup.

In addition to explaining those bets, we provide valuable Super Bowl historical information and relevant Super Bowl betting trends for many of them, as well as updated odds when they become available.

The implied probability is calculated directly from the listed odds and reflects how the sportsbook prices each team before accounting for its built-in margin. Because sportsbooks include this margin, the implied probabilities for all teams combined add up to more than 100%.

The true probability column adjusts those implied percentages so that all teams together equal exactly 100%. This removes the sportsbook’s edge and shows each team’s relative chance of winning Super Bowl 60 based purely on the current market.

Comparing implied probability to true probability can help bettors better understand where value may exist in Super Bowl futures. Teams with shorter odds carry a larger share of the market’s expectation, while longshots may offer bigger payouts but much lower realistic chances of lifting the Lombardi Trophy.

Super Bowl MVP Betting

In each Super Bowl, a standout performer receives the Super Bowl Most Valuable Player award.

To date, only once has the MVP not come from the winning team. In Super Bowl V, the Baltimore Colts (now Indianapolis Colts) defeated the Dallas Cowboys 16-13, but Cowboys linebacker Chuck Howley earned Super Bowl MVP honors.

The record for most Super Bowl MVP wins is five, which belongs to Tom Brady. Brady won the award four times with the New England Patriots and earned his fifth when the Bucs defeated the Chiefs in Super Bowl 55.

Brady, Joe Montana (three, all with the San Francisco 49ers), and Patrick Mahomes (three) are the only three players to be named Super Bowl MVP more than twice.

Overall, the award has been dominated by quarterbacks, who have taken home Super Bowl MVP honors 34 times in 59 games.

Super Bowl Sides and Totals

There are many ways to bet on the Super Bowl. But as is the case with other NFL games, Super Bowl betting starts with moneyline, point spread, and total bets that are centered around the outcome and result of the game.

Moneyline and spread odds are known as sides, and Super Bowl sides receive a lot of action on both teams. Many Super Bowl bettors who are new bettors or only bet on the NFL every now and then like to bet on the outcome of the game.

Total betting, which is also known as over/under betting, is the other primary way to bet on the Super Bowl.

  • Super Bowl Spread Betting →
  • Super Bowl Over/Under Betting →

Super Bowl Prop Bets

Super Bowl props generate heavy interest every year, and that will not be waning anytime soon.

In fact, the outcome of Super Bowl props can be more interesting than the game outcome, especially for neutrals.

Super Bowl Player Props

The most notable kind of NFL props are NFL player props. Sportsbooks offer many player props for NFL games throughout the season, including the playoffs and Super Bowl.

Prop betting originated with the Super Bowl. The first prop bet ever offered was for William “Refrigerator” Perry of the Chicago Bears to score a touchdown in Super Bowl XX against the New England Patriots.

So, it is only fitting that the Super Bowl prop paradise. Here are some examples of the Super Bowl player props that you will see at many online sports betting sites.

  • What will be the total number of passing yards or pass completions for each quarterback?
  • How many touchdowns or interceptions will be thrown?
  • Who will throw the first interception?
  • How many rushing yards or rushing attempts will the running backs have?
  • How many catches or receiving yards will pass-catchers have?
  • Which player(s) will score a touchdown?
  • Who will score the first touchdown?

Also, a special occasion calls for some player prop options that may only be available for the Super Bowl. Some of those options are cross-sport props. Super Bowl cross-sport props combine Super Bowl player props with props from other events, such as NBA or NHL games taking place on Super Bowl Sunday.

  • Super Bowl Player Prop Betting →

Super Bowl Touchdown Scorer Odds

Most NFL player props are over/under bets, but there are many options that aren’t.

First and anytime touchdown scorer bets are among the player prop odds that aren’t over/under odds.

They are especially popular during the Super Bowl, when many exciting viewers will be hoping to see their favorite player score a touchdown in the biggest game of the season.

  • Super Bowl First & Anytime Touchdown Scorer Betting →

Super Bowl First Score Betting

Along with betting on Super Bowl touchdown scorers, you can also bet on what and when the first scoring play in this year’s Super Bowl will be.

Will it be a touchdown, a field goal, a defensive touchdown, or a safety? Most importantly, will the team that scores first in the Super Bowl go on to win the game?

Through last season’s championship clash, the team to score first in the Super Bowl has gone on to win the game 38 of 59 times (64.4%).

That is an impressive percentage, which means that even if one of your Super Bowl first score bets don’t work out, some in-game action might be in the cards if the odds are right.

  • Super Bowl First Score Betting →

Super Bowl Novelty Bets

Coin Toss Odds

Will it be heads? Will it be tails?

The coin toss means a lot in any football game, but the Super Bowl coin toss carries even more significance. The team that wins the coin toss can set the tone offensively or defensively out of the gate and lay the foundation for a memorable Super Bowl win.

For that reason, the Super Bowl coin toss is another popular prop option for the game.

Unlike many other Super Bowl 60 bets, coin toss betting is indeed a real toss-up (pun intended). That is because there are matching odds for both heads and tails.

  • Super Bowl Coin Toss Betting & History →

Gatorade Color Odds

Gatorade showers are a frequent feature of celebrations at the end of major sporting events, huge upsets, or exciting finishes.

Due to the large number of bets placed on the winning Gatorade color, the Super Bowl Gatorade shower is one of the most anticipated moments of the night.

Because of the nature of Gatorade color betting, it shouldn’t be taken as seriously as other options. That said, it is still taken very seriously.

  • Super Bowl Gatorade Color Betting & History →

Super Bowl National Anthem Betting

In 1931, “The Star-Spangled Banner” was adopted as the official national anthem of the United States. These days, the anthem is a regular feature at sporting events across the country. For example, if you go to an MLB, NBA, NFL, or a college football game, you will hear the anthem performed beforehand.

Arguably the most notable national anthem performance takes place at the Super Bowl. Each year, a major musical artist performs the anthem before the action gets underway.

Over/under bets on the performance’s length are the main way to bet on the Super Bowl national anthem. The set total can vary depending on the performer, but many anthem performances are around or under the two-minute mark.

Additionally, Lucky Rebel, BetOnline, and other Super Bowl betting sites offer odds on the anthem performer’s attire, whether the anthem performer will forget part of the lyrics, who will be shown on the TV screen during the performance, and which of the shortest scoring drive of the Super Bowl will or anthem performance will be longer.

  • Super Bowl National Anthem Over/Under Betting →

Super Bowl Halftime Show Odds

Often enough, halftime is a good opportunity to get up and stretch your legs, get something to eat or drink, and perhaps make a few live bets.

Many people do indeed use halftime of the Super Bowl for that purpose. But for many others, there is a different reason to get up and move around during the break.

That would be the Super Bowl halftime show, which is always a major spectacle.

Some of the artists and music groups to perform at the Super Bowl halftime show include illustrious names such as Michael Jackson, Diana Ross, Aerosmith, Paul McCartney, Madonna, Beyonce, and Kendrick Lamar, who performed at Super Bowl 59 in New Orleans. At Super Bowl 60, Bad Bunny will perform the halftime show.

What are some of the Super Bowl halftime show betting odds you can bet on at sites such as Lucky Rebel?

  • Which guests will feature in the halftime show performance?
  • Which songs will the halftime show start and end with?
  • What words or phrases will the halftime show performer(s) say during the performance?

Those are just a few of the numerous options potentially available at sportsbooks that offer Super Bowl halftime show odds.

  • Super Bowl Halftime Show Betting →

Super Bowl Commercial Odds

Along with the Super Bowl halftime show, the Super Bowl ads are one of the most anticipated parts of the evening that don’t involve the game action. With so many viewers watching, companies shell out millions of dollars to get some of the spotlight in the hope of a major return on their investment.

There have been many memorable Super Bowl ads over the years for varying reasons. Some of the best Super Bowl ads from many years ago are still talked about in the present. With limited time to make a big impression, companies get rather creative with what they do to try to grab attention.

Unlike a lot of other Super Bowl betting options, Super Bowl commercial odds are not universally available. But at betting sites that do have those odds, you can bet on some very interesting selections.

FAQ

Super Bowl Betting FAQ
What is the Super Bowl?
The Super Bowl is the NFL’s championship game. It is played between the champions of the league’s two conferences, the AFC and NFC.
When and where is the next Super Bowl?
Super Bowl 60, the championship game for the 2025 NFL season, will take place on Sunday, February 8, 2026. It will be played at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California. Levi’s Stadium is the home of the San Francisco 49ers.
What kind of Super Bowl bets can I place?
There are many Super Bowl betting options. Moneyline betting, spread betting, and total betting are the most popular Super Bowl betting options. Super Bowl player prop betting is also very popular. Many sports betting sites also offer options like coin toss odds, Gatorade color odds, and national anthem odds.
Who should I bet on to win this year's Super Bowl?
Well, we can’t make your decision for you. But Betting News will provide a number of articles and resources to help you make the most informed Super Bowl 60 bets possible.
How do I bet on the Super Bowl?
You can place bets on the Super Bowl at any sportsbook that offers Super Bowl betting odds.
